newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Marlin sees growth in beneficiation.
newsitem.headline: Marlin sees growth in beneficiation.

text.p: Marlin Corporation Ltd said on Thursday growth in the granite business in South Africa lay in the beneficiation process and not in production.

Mario Marcenaro, director of Marlin and the South African representative of IIE S.a.R.L., said South Africa had increased its output of granite in the past six years but lagged behind as far as beneficiation was concerned.
"There is strong growth not in production but beneficiation. South Africa was not well planned to take advantage of the high production (of granite)," Marcenaro told reporters and analysts.

Marlin and Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Thursday that Marlin would acquire 56 percent of Kudu Granite Holdings Ltd and other assets from Deutsche Steinindustrie AG for 56 million rand creating one of the largest granite block producers in the world.

They said the acquisition saw Marlin's ultimate holding compay, IIE, buying Deutsche Steinindustrie AG's (Destag) southern African assets which included its 56 percent stake in and loans to Kudu and its subsidiaries.
IIE would also buy a 33.3 percent stake in Natural Stone Processors (NSP) (Pty) Ltd. NSP operates a beneficiation plant producing granite slabs.
Marcenaro said with the acquisition of NSP its unit Minaco would focus mainly on beneficiation and Marlin Corporation on other business.

He said beneficiation could add value of up to four times to a granite block. Transport costs would also be reduced due to beneficiation being closer to the source instead of exporting most of the granite blocks.

Marcenaro said the cost of Kudu was first put at 165 cents per Kudu share but was reduced to 100 cents a share after a due diligence study revealed that Kudu had a problem maintaining its debt of 60 million rand and a debt of 11 million not reflected in the balance sheet.
He said it was the Marlin policy not to have financial gearing and hence it would make a rights offer to reduce debt.
"Kudu's debt will have to be reduced. A rights issue has been planned to raise that amount. Final parameters (of the issue) will be available shortly," Marcenaro said.

Marcenaro said the acquisition of Kudu would increase their market share of granite in South Africa, enhance the long term reserves of Kudu and build on Kudu's product reputation. He said Marlin would also attain critical mass which would assist in expansion plans.
Following the acquisition Marcenaro said the Marlin group would have to be restructured and one option would be to split the beneficiation and operational units.
Anglo American has a 30 percent stake in IIE and an eight percent indirect interest in Marlin.
David Fish, director of Anglo's new mining business division, said it would assist Marlin with technical expertise and collaboration on mineral rights.
